name: CSSI
summary: Its public materials describe cost segregation and specialty property-tax services.
fit: Property owners seeking a specialist for the study portion of a tax project
scenario: You have a candidate property and a CPA, but need to clarify who prepares the study and who implements the tax reporting.
decision: Ask for the study methodology, required property records, and the precise handoff to your CPA.
question: What deliverables will my return preparer receive?

name: Capstan Tax Strategies
summary: Its public materials describe cost segregation, energy-related incentives, and other specialty tax services.
fit: Owners comparing technical property studies and related incentive opportunities
scenario: Your building project could involve more than depreciation, so the service proposal needs to distinguish each technical analysis.
decision: Ask which specialty services are included and how results are coordinated with your broader tax plan.
question: Which analyses are separate from the cost segregation study?

name: Cost Seg Smart
summary: Publishes property-specific cost segregation reports with CPA coordination and written support.
fit: Owners considering a digital study workflow
scenario: You want a convenient report but need to understand the inputs, review process, and reporting support before purchase.
decision: Ask how unusual property features, renovations, and incomplete records are handled.
question: Who reviews the property facts behind the generated report?
note: Cost Seg Smart markets a complete service, not just software. Its published materials distinguish residential, STR and commercial offerings and separately available Form 3115 preparation. Compare the actual property tier, review process and filing responsibilities rather than assuming an online order is an unreviewed report.

name: Engineered Tax Services
summary: Its public materials describe cost segregation and specialty tax services, including energy and research-related incentives.
fit: Owners and businesses comparing multiple specialty tax projects
scenario: You have a property study need and another potential incentive, but they may require different evidence and engagements.
decision: Ask how each specialty project is scoped and which professional coordinates it with your tax return.
question: Which project needs to be completed first to meet my deadline?

name: KBKG
summary: Its public materials describe tax-credit and incentive consulting, including cost segregation.
fit: Businesses and property owners seeking technical specialty tax support
scenario: You want to compare a specialty-tax engagement with a household or business-wide planning engagement.
decision: Ask what technical deliverables the quote includes and whether broader planning is separately available.
question: Where does the specialty engagement end and broader tax planning begin?
note: KBKG publishes specialist cost segregation services and links to residential software at CostSegregation.com. Compare the actual product and team rather than treating a software subscription and a specialist engagement as interchangeable.

name: Madison SPECS
summary: Its public materials describe national cost segregation services with engineering and CPA involvement.
fit: Owners seeking a property-study specialist and CPA coordination
scenario: You want a feasibility review before deciding which properties deserve a full study.
decision: Ask how the preliminary estimate differs from the final report and what your CPA needs for implementation.
question: What information can change the preliminary benefit estimate?

name: RE Cost Seg
summary: R.E. Cost Seg distinguishes Rapid Reports without a site visit from a Fully Engineered service with a virtual visit, and describes a report plus fixed asset schedule for the CPA.
fit: Rental owners comparing specialist study services
scenario: You want to understand how a remote information-gathering process handles property-specific details.
decision: Identify the exact report product, property eligibility, review professional and included site evidence before comparing fees.
question: Which records are needed beyond square footage and purchase price?
note: A Rapid Report and a Fully Engineered engagement are different workflows. Ask which product the quote covers and how acquired furnishings or later renovations are handled.

name: BASIS Cost Segregation
summary: Its public materials describe a technology-supported residential cost segregation workflow.
fit: Residential investors evaluating an app-based study process
scenario: You want to compare a residential study workflow with a full review of your ability to use the resulting deductions.
decision: Ask which property types the product supports and who evaluates reporting and owner-level eligibility.
question: Does the service include analysis of my ability to use the deduction?
note: BASIS describes an online residential study workflow with professional review and a report for the buyer's CPA. Map the process from property questionnaire to supporting uploads to the final reviewed deliverable. Ask what happens when the intake reveals renovations or missing acquisition records. AE is a separate candidate for owner-level planning and implementation; a residential report purchase need not replace a trusted preparer. Compare the study product and the advisory project as separate purchases.

name: Cost Seg Atlas
summary: Its public materials describe educational cost segregation analyses and optional technical-review services.
fit: Owners exploring a preliminary analysis before purchasing a formal study
scenario: You are evaluating a tool that expressly distinguishes an educational analysis from a signed technical study.
decision: Ask what document you receive, what review upgrades are available, and whether your CPA will accept the deliverable.
question: Am I buying an educational analysis or an implementation-ready study?
note: The pricing page expressly describes educational analyses, not signed studies, and labels professional review as paused. Confirm the independent completion and review work needed for the intended filing use.

name: Cost Segregation Authority
summary: Its public materials describe cost segregation and related specialty property-tax services.
fit: Owners comparing a property-focused specialty tax provider
scenario: You want a study but also need to understand what related services the proposal actually includes.
decision: Ask which property-tax projects, reporting tasks, and support terms are expressly included.
question: Does the quote include any work beyond the property study?

name: Cost Segregation Guys
summary: Its public materials describe cost segregation and related services, including Form 3115 and energy-related work.
fit: Property owners seeking a specialist for studies and associated technical tasks
scenario: Your property was acquired in an earlier year and the implementation question may differ from a current acquisition.
decision: Ask how older-property studies and any accounting-method work are coordinated with the return preparer.
question: Who is responsible for determining and preparing the reporting method?
note: Cost Segregation Guys describes virtual or in-person study options and a report with a fixed-asset schedule for the client’s CPA. Its resource menu also includes Form 3115 information. Ask which reporting tasks are actually contracted, instead of treating a resource link as either proof of inclusion or proof of exclusion. For a property owner retaining a preparer, make report acceptance and correction support explicit. Compare AE on the separately scoped owner analysis and implementation; the engineering project and wider tax engagement need different deliverables.

name: CostSeg Express
summary: Its public materials describe a fast digital cost segregation workflow marketed to rental owners.
fit: Short-term rental owners prioritizing study delivery speed
scenario: You want a quick report but have not yet established how rental-activity rules affect your tax position.
decision: Ask how the report is reviewed and arrange a separate facts-based eligibility analysis before relying on projected savings.
question: Who evaluates participation and deduction usability before I rely on the estimate?
note: The public offer is described as a technology-assisted planning study. Clarify who updates final acquisition facts and performs the professional review before a filing position is taken.

name: CostSegEZ
summary: Its public materials describe an online cost segregation reporting workflow.
fit: Investors considering a streamlined digital report process
scenario: You are comparing convenient online delivery with the amount of property documentation your situation requires.
decision: Ask what review occurs when renovation costs or property details do not fit standard inputs.
question: How are unusual property features and renovations reviewed?
note: CostSegEZ describes instant generation with a review option. Specify whether you want preliminary information, a final report, or a reviewed report accepted by your preparer. Compare those deliverables individually before comparing price. An owner with several properties should check whether review and corrections apply to every address or only the selected order. Ask AE for a property-by-property scope if the desired work includes both study coordination and owner-level planning. Avoid interpreting automated delivery as a statement about return preparation.

name: CostSegRx
summary: Its public materials describe cost segregation studies with a published FAQ addressing scope and required inputs.
fit: Owners who want to understand study requirements before ordering
scenario: Your land allocation and existing depreciation records need attention before a study can be implemented.
decision: Ask which basis inputs you must supply and which analyses are outside the study's stated scope.
question: Who is responsible for reviewing the land allocation?
note: Its FAQ says the provider does not determine the owner’s land allocation or real-estate cost basis. Resolve those inputs with the appropriate professional before comparing projected results.

name: CostSegregation.com
summary: Its public materials describe self-guided cost segregation software for eligible property projects.
fit: Owners considering a software-led approach to organizing a study
scenario: You have a straightforward property but want your CPA to evaluate whether the software output suits the project.
decision: Ask about supported property types, input requirements, professional review, and CPA handoff.
question: Will my CPA review the proposed output before I purchase?
note: KBKG links to CostSegregation.com as residential software. Confirm current product ownership and support; these are related research paths, not necessarily independent provider choices.

name: Duffy + Duffy Cost Segregation
summary: Its public materials describe engineering-based cost segregation with property-study services across states.
fit: Commercial and residential owners comparing a technical study provider
scenario: You have construction plans and invoices and want to know how a detailed technical review would use them.
decision: Ask which site information and cost records support the study and what deliverables reach the CPA.
question: How will construction records affect the study methodology?
note: For Duffy + Duffy, compare the engineering assignment at the property level: plans, invoices, site information, and the intended report recipient. A new-construction project with detailed cost records requires a different intake conversation from an acquired building with limited documentation. Ask which evidence will actually be reviewed and how unresolved items are communicated. AE's owner-level scope should identify the separate analysis and reporting work needed after delivery. A construction-focused study and a household planning engagement can be complementary.

name: ICS Tax
summary: Its public materials describe cost segregation, fixed-asset, accounting-method, and other specialty tax services.
fit: Businesses and advisers seeking technical help with asset-related projects
scenario: Your asset records include prior-year changes and a new project that require separate technical analyses.
decision: Ask which fixed-asset and accounting-method tasks are included and what your filing team must supply.
question: How will the study be reconciled to my existing fixed-asset ledger?
note: ICS Tax describes fixed-asset and accounting-method services alongside specialty tax projects. An owner reviewing old schedules should identify the particular ledger issue, the proposed correction, and the new property analysis as separate assignments. Ask who reconciles historic records and who determines the return implementation. AE's planning proposal should explain how specialist findings feed into the wider owner forecast. Comparing a specialty calculation with a complete planning engagement obscures the handoff; keep the technical and advisory deliverables separately priced.

name: MSC Tax
summary: Its public materials describe cost segregation and specialty tax services for real estate and business projects.
fit: Owners evaluating technical property and incentive analyses
scenario: Your project may involve a study plus another specialty tax service with a different evidence requirement.
decision: Ask for separate deliverables and responsibilities for each technical project.
question: Which analyses require additional records beyond the study inputs?
note: MSC Tax's specialty-property work can intersect with other incentive projects. Request a separate evidence list, deliverable, and responsible professional for each analysis. A document collected for a property study may not answer the questions posed by a different incentive engagement. Compare AE on the owner-level review it actually offers, and decide whether a specialist remains necessary. The selection should clarify how reports reach the filing team and which assumptions need to be reconciled before the combined plan is used.

name: Maven Cost Segregation
summary: Maven describes engineering professionals physically inspecting properties, report delivery within 30 days of the site visit and coordination with the existing CPA.
fit: Owners comparing detailed study and reporting-support options
scenario: Your existing property has a long depreciation history that must be reconciled before implementation.
decision: Confirm property access, the evidence collected, delivery dependencies and the written support terms.
question: Who validates the old schedules before applying the study results?
note: The 30-day period is Maven’s published target after the site visit, not an independently measured delivery result. Compare the date the clock starts and what missing records do to the schedule.

name: McGuire Sponsel
summary: Its public materials describe cost segregation, fixed-asset, research, and other specialty tax advisory services.
fit: Businesses seeking project-specific technical tax support
scenario: Your company needs a specialist project while owner-level planning remains with another adviser.
decision: Ask how the specialty team communicates assumptions and deliverables to the broader planning team.
question: What handoff documentation will my existing advisers receive?
note: McGuire Sponsel describes technical specialties delivered in collaboration with CPA and real estate professionals. If your existing CPA is managing the relationship, ask whether you or that CPA contracts for the specialty project and receives the final work. Compare AE's direct advisory engagement as a different contracting arrangement. The important handoff includes assumptions, calculations, unresolved evidence, and the reporting deadline. Multiple advisers can work effectively together when the engagement identifies the coordinator rather than assuming the specialist replaces the whole tax team.

name: My Cost Segregation
summary: Its public materials describe cost segregation services with published pricing and support information.
fit: Property owners seeking visibility into study scope and quoted fees
scenario: You want to compare a published study price with a proposal that includes additional advisory or reporting work.
decision: Ask what the quoted price includes and whether preparer coordination or reporting work costs extra.
question: Which deliverables and support terms are covered by the study price?
note: My Cost Segregation describes several study tiers with different review and support terms. Identify the property value and complexity before comparing its published product options. Ask which tier handles exceptions, who signs the report, and what conditions govern support. AE should quote study work separately from broader advice. A lower-priced self-service option and a professionally reviewed project are different purchases; the right comparison includes the client's input work, the preparer's acceptance, and the extra help needed after the initial delivery.

name: Source Advisors
summary: Publishes cost segregation services alongside other specialty tax offerings.
fit: Commercial owners comparing property analysis and additional incentive work
scenario: You own several commercial buildings and need to decide whether depreciation analysis and other incentive studies belong in one coordinated engagement.
decision: Separate each project’s scope, evidence, fee and report before comparing a combined proposal.
question: Which team owns the fixed-asset handoff across the different specialty projects?
note: Bedford joined Source Advisors; compare current engagement teams rather than assuming the brands are unrelated.

name: Bedford Cost Segregation
summary: Source Advisors announced its combination with Bedford in May 2021.
fit: Owners researching a legacy Bedford referral or proposal
scenario: Your CPA referred you to Bedford, but the current engagement may be offered through Source Advisors.
decision: Confirm the current contracting entity, team and support responsibility before comparing an older brochure.
question: Who contracts for, signs and supports a current Bedford-related study?
note: This is a legacy-brand research path. Bedford and Source Advisors are not presented as two independent alternatives.

name: Seneca Cost Segregation
summary: Seneca describes engineering-based studies, virtual site visits, a PDF report and a fixed asset schedule for the owner’s CPA.
fit: Rental and commercial owners comparing a study, CPA handoff and conditional audit-support terms
scenario: Your furnished rental needs a supported component analysis and a clear agreement about what happens if a study conclusion is questioned.
decision: Compare technical review, fixed asset delivery and the exact examination-support obligations before choosing.
question: What does AuditDefense cover, and which conditions apply to the study-fee refund?
note: Seneca’s advertised refund is conditional, including a greater-than-5% depreciation adjustment caused by Seneca. A refund of study fees is different from coverage of tax, penalties or all representation expenses.

name: RentalWriteOff
summary: Describes rental-property studies with asset CSVs, methodology files and photo documentation.
fit: Rental owners comparing final report formats and digital records
scenario: Your CPA needs an itemized asset file and photographs that reconcile to the final report.
decision: Compare the delivered files and correction process using your preparer’s actual import requirements.
question: Can my preparer reconcile the CSV, photographs and final report without re-entering every asset?
note: Ask to see a sample deliverable and confirm eligibility for the actual property.

name: Remote Cost Seg
summary: Publishes a remote cost segregation service workflow.
fit: Owners considering a study without a conventional travel-based intake
scenario: You manage rentals in multiple states and need to compare remote evidence collection with site access arrangements.
decision: Clarify the owner’s responsibilities for images, measurements and access before accepting a delivery target.
question: Who supplies missing physical evidence, and how does that affect timing?
note: Confirm current inspection requirements directly; remote delivery does not establish the review scope.

name: Unlevered
summary: Describes rental-home and STR studies and makes a sample study available.
fit: Owners who want to examine a report before selecting a rental study
scenario: You have two provider proposals but want your CPA to review a sample report before committing.
decision: Compare reconciliation, cost detail, reviewer identification and supporting files in actual samples.
question: How closely will my report follow the sample and what changes for unusual property facts?
note: A sample report illustrates format; it does not establish the eventual result for your building.

name: BDO USA
summary: Publishes a cost segregation calculator and describes an engineering, construction and CPA team.
fit: Owners considering a commercial project within a broader accounting relationship
scenario: Your company already uses an accounting firm and needs a property study to fit its fixed-asset and tax-reporting process.
decision: Distinguish an illustrative calculator result from the contracted study and implementation deliverables.
question: Which professionals perform the final property analysis after the preliminary estimate?
note: A calculator is a feasibility tool, not the final study or a quote.

name: Cherry Bekaert
summary: Describes combined engineering and tax services, including property inspection and report delivery.
fit: Commercial and residential owners comparing engineering and tax coordination
scenario: Your acquisition and renovation overlap, so the study and tax team need an agreed cost boundary before work starts.
decision: Ask how acquisition costs, subsequent work and any prior-year implementation are separately documented.
question: Does the proposal identify inspection, study review and accounting-method responsibilities separately?
note: Confirm whether accounting-method preparation and filing are included in your actual engagement.

name: Baker Tilly
summary: Describes cost segregation alongside fixed-asset, repair and related incentive services.
fit: Owners whose property analysis intersects with repairs, disposals or other incentives
scenario: Your business has a renovation ledger, removed equipment and an existing fixed-asset register that need coordinated review.
decision: Compare the study boundary with repair, disposal and fixed-asset projects before combining fees.
question: Which analyses are separate deliverables, and how are overlapping costs reconciled?
note: Confirm the current assigned team and relevant property experience rather than relying on the broad service menu.

name: CLA (CliftonLarsonAllen)
summary: Describes cost segregation with tax and engineering perspectives across multiple building types.
fit: Owners comparing property studies within a broader tax and accounting engagement
scenario: You operate a specialized building and need the study team to distinguish ordinary building systems from business equipment.
decision: Request experience with the relevant building use and a clear map of technical and filing responsibilities.
question: How will the team document business-specific functions and shared systems?
note: Request a property-specific scope; a published industry list does not confirm staffing for your engagement.
